headline_marked: [[Nepal flood death toll rises to 633]], nearly 3,000 missing as rescuers battle to find survivors
headline: Nepal flood death toll rises to 633, nearly 3,000 missing as rescuers battle to find survivors
summary: Rescuers are still searching for thousands missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan region, engulfing villages. The death toll is expected to rise further.
details: Rescuers in Nepal and China are still battling to locate nearly 3,000 people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan region. The disaster has engulfed villages and led to 633 bodies being recovered so far. Some bodies may have been swept downstream as far as India.

Nepal's disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing persons list that already included trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash. The trauma of Wednesday's catastrophe has been "enormous," with up to 93,000 people potentially affected, according to the Red Cross.

Survivors describe losing everything and face an agonizing wait for news of loved ones, along with the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing. One survivor, Buddhi Ram Dangol, stated, "All the settlements near the river were swept away. There is nothing left."

Emergency teams are racing to retrieve survivors from affected zones where widespread devastation means food and water supplies are running out. Compounding the search efforts are fears of further flooding, as the deluge of ice and mud caused huge lakes to form.

Nepali police urged all rescuers to "immediately move to a safe location" after receiving information that "a water dam has burst again on the Tibetan side." In Tibet, Chinese authorities temporarily suspended rescue operations in the hardest-hit area of Gyirong due to renewed flood risks.

On the Nepali side, the military located people trapped in the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project and are working to extract them. Around 350 workers and residents have been brought to safety from the site, but efforts continue for over a hundred still trapped.

Workers rescued from other dam projects along the Trishuli valley described the disaster unfolding with terrifying speed. Buddha Tamang survived only because he was inside a tunnel when the flood struck, noting that "senior officers working on the other side, they were all swept away."

Among the missing are 2,426 people in Nepal, including hundreds of foreigners, and 554 in Tibet, where seven deaths have been reported. Scores of Hindu devotees on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash are also among those unaccounted for.

headline_marked: [[Road repairs trigger long tailback]] on Dhaka-Chattogram highway, stranding thousands
headline: Road repairs trigger long tailback on Dhaka-Chattogram highway, stranding thousands
summary: Emergency repair work on Ashariarchar Bridge in Narayanganj led to the closure of one lane on the Dhaka-bound side of the Dhaka-Chattogram highway. This caused severe tailbacks, leaving thousands of commuters stranded for hours.
details: A severe traffic congestion developed on the Dhaka-bound lane of the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, stretching from Daudkandi in Cumilla to the Meghna Toll Plaza. This was caused by emergency repair work on the Ashariarchar Bridge in Sonargaon, Narayanganj, stranding thousands of passengers for hours.

The Roads and Highways Department initiated repairs on a large pothole on the Ashariarchar Bridge that posed an accident risk. One of the two lanes was closed for this work, with vehicles alternately using the other lane.

The congestion, which began last night, saw traffic moving very slowly or at a standstill in most sections between Daudkandi and Meghna Toll Plaza. The situation worsened at night as a large number of vehicles attempted to pass through the single operational lane.

Commuters reported being stuck for around three hours, with many journeys taking nearly twice as long as usual. Families traveling with children faced particular hardship amid the prolonged delays and hot weather.

Officer-in-charge of Daudkandi Highway Police Station, Prem Das Roy, confirmed that highway police teams are continuously working on the ground. Their efforts aim to ease traffic movement and control the congestion.
